content.text:
Actually row6 col4 is 0, so it bridges the top and bottom sections into one single connected component instead of two. Let me count up all the cyan cells across each row to get the total.

Total comes to 45 cyan cells out of 91 non-orange cells, and I'm filling them from the bottom up: rows 9, 8, and 7 take 30 cells, leaving 15. Row 6 only has one available slot (col 4) since the rest is orange, leaving 14; row 5's full width of 10 anchors on that column and uses up the remainder down to 4; and row 4 fills the 4 cells closest to the center of the anchors from row 5, giving columns 3, 4, 5, 6 in priority order based on distance from center.

I'm counting the cyan cells row by row, getting totals of 8, 8, 9, 1, and 6 across the rows, summing to 32, and confirming they form one connected component within the 12x9 grid.

Since 108 minus the 8 orange cells gives 100 non-orange cells, I'm filling rows 11, 10, 9 completely (27 cells) then need 5 more cells in row 8, choosing columns closest to the weighted center of the cyan mass (around column 3.94), which gives columns 4, 3, 5, 2, 6 as the fill order.
